description: The line plot illustrates the GPU memory cost (in GB) as a function of the number of video frames processed, comparing five different video understanding models: VideoLLaMB, VideoLLaMB-R, PLLaVA, LLaVA-NeXT, and VideoLLaVA. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Frames,” spans from 0 to 1000 in linear scale with major gridlines at intervals of 200. The y-axis, labeled “Memory (GB),” ranges from 0 to 400 in linear scale with major gridlines every 50 GB. VideoLLaVA (purple line with circle markers) exhibits a steeply increasing memory cost, starting near 20 GB at 0 frames and rising sharply to over 400 GB by 300 frames. In contrast, VideoLLaMB (pink line with circle markers) and VideoLLaMB-R (brown line with circle markers) show nearly flat memory usage, remaining below 30 GB across all frame counts. PLLaVA (green line with circle markers) and LLaVA-NeXT (cyan line with circle markers) demonstrate moderate, roughly linear increases: PLLaVA rises from ~20 GB to ~75 GB, while LLaVA-NeXT climbs from ~20 GB to ~145 GB over 1000 frames. All lines are solid, and markers are consistently placed at data points. The plot highlights the significant memory efficiency of VideoLLaMB variants compared to the others, especially VideoLLaVA, under increasing video length.
